newsitem.title: USA: Graco Inc sees improved performance in 97.
newsitem.headline: Graco Inc sees improved performance in 97.

text.p: Graco Inc said that, despite unfavorable exchange rates in the first quarter, it remains optimistic about improved financial performance for the year.

"We are encouraged by our order levels heading into the second quarter," George Aristides, president, said in a statement. "Graco expects to introduce a number of new products in 1997 and our continued investments in product development, marketing, and manufacturing should have a positive impact on the company in 1997 and our long-term ability to grow profitability."
Earlier, Graco reported net earnings of $6.2 million, or $0.35 a share, a first quarter record, up from last year's $5.6 million or $0.32 a share.

Graco said its first quarter operating results included income from the sale of its Franklin Park, Illinois. That completed the relocation of its industrial systems engineering and sales expertise to Minneapolis.
Graco said worldwide industrial/automotive equipment sales increased six percent from a year ago, while lubrication equipment sales rose six percent. Contractor equipment sales fell four percent.

"Although sales in the contractor equipment business were slow in the first two months of the year, the month of March was strong and recent order trends support our positive view for the remainder of the year," Aristides said. "Our backlog of $26.4 million has grown $7.3 million since the beginning of 1997."
Graco makes systems and equipment to move, measure, control, dispense and apply fluid materials.
